proposed.text: What is the maximum ramp run between landings under BP 344 Philippine standard, and how does this differ from the U.S. ADA figure that is commonly misapplied?

options.text: Philippines: 9000 mm maximum; U.S. ADA: 10500 mm — the Philippine standard is more restrictive
Philippines: 10500 mm maximum; U.S. ADA: 9000 mm — the Philippine standard allows longer runs
Philippines: 7500 mm maximum; U.S. ADA: 9000 mm — both standards require landings more frequently than most reviewers teach
Philippines: 10500 mm maximum; U.S. ADA: 10500 mm — both standards use the same maximum ramp run length

rationale.summary: Trap #2: Philippines (BP 344) allows 10500 mm maximum ramp run; U.S. ADA uses 9000 mm.
rationale.explanation: Trap #2 in the article. Philippine BP 344 IRR specifies a maximum ramp run of 10,500 mm (10.5 m) before a rest landing is required. U.S. ADA specifies 9,000 mm (9 m). Philippine reviewers often incorrectly cite the ADA figure of 9 m. The Philippine standard actually allows longer runs than ADA. This is counterintuitive — many assume the Philippine standard would be equal or more restrictive, but the 10.5 m figure is the correct Philippine value.
common_misconceptions: Using the ADA's 9000 mm figure as the Philippine standard — BP 344 specifies the longer 10500 mm
Assuming Philippine standards are always more restrictive than ADA — the ramp run maximum is actually more permissive

proposed.explanation: Philippines: 10500 mm max ramp run (not the ADA's 9000 mm) — a frequently misapplied foreign standard.
